generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The removal of the `assert path.isAbsolute()` / `assert relativePath.isAbsolute() == false` guards in `FilesEntitlement` is paired with the deletion of the two parser-level validation tests (`testEntitlementRelativePathWhenAbsolute` and `testEntitlementAbsolutePathWhenRelative`). Taken together, this means there is no longer any visible enforcement that a `path` entry is absolute or a `relative_path` entry is relative. If the validation logic was intentionally removed (e.g., because it was unsound on Windows where `/foo` is not absolute), that is reasonable—but it would be worth confirming that no other layer (e.g., the `PolicyParser` or `FilesEntitlement.build`) still rejects malformed entries, since a silently-accepted misconfigured policy is harder to diagnose at runtime than a parse-time error.

`testPathToReadDir` is created via `createTempDir()` inside the test method body, while `TEST_ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO_FILE` is a `@BeforeClass`-initialized static. For consistency and to avoid creating a new temp directory on every invocation (e.g., if the test is retried), consider promoting `testPathToReadDir` to a static field initialized in `beforeClass()` alongside `TEST_ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO_FILE`.

review_comment: Why do we need to remove these asserts? We can specify absolute and relative paths in Windows. I don't think we should add leniency to make windows testing easier, let's adjust the tests so they aren't assuming `/` is the root path.
It's in the description; the tests are fixed, but the asserts will fail anyway in production code because we have unix paths in policies with a cluster running on windows and vice-versa.

I think we can solve the eg `/proc/meminfo` in a different way: we don't need to add those to the policy on windows. Relaxing the assertions make it unclear why `path` and `relative_path` exist when there is no enforcement on what exists there.
Also, if for some reason we needed to support skipping certain file entitlements on different platforms in policy files, we could do that with an additional file property.

There will always be the matter of policy files; unless we add platform-specific sections to them, we may end up with a mix of absolute paths for different platforms.
I don't think we want that complication (platform-specific sections); if we do, we can address this separately.
